title: Synapse GoInbound Worker
description: Front door for inbound /send: EDU-only transactions answered natively, everything else proxied to the Python inbound worker.

list.name: bucket
list.label: Bucket
list.description: Range window for rate() and histogram_quantile(). Prometheus scrapes every 15s, so 30s is the floor.

list.name: synapse_server
list.label: Synapse server_name
list.description: server_name label on Synapse's own metrics; the inbound-federation job also scrapes other homeservers.

panels.title: Modes
panels.description: What each kind of payload does, from modes.edu and modes.pdu in goinbound-worker.yaml.

panels.title: Transactions/s
panels.description: Every /send this worker received, whatever it did with it.

panels.title: Answered natively
panels.description: Share of transactions answered here instead of by the Python worker. About 96% is the ceiling on this homeserver; 0 in proxy and shadow mode.

panels.title: Would answer natively
panels.description: Shadow mode: share of evaluated transactions native mode would have answered.

panels.title: Shadow disagreements (window)
panels.description: Transactions we would have answered 200 that Synapse answered otherwise. A 429 is usually Synapse refusing a concurrent transaction, which our own claim would refuse too; anything else deserves a look in the logs.

panels.title: Forward failures (window)
panels.description: EDUs that could not be handed to their stream writer. Each fails its transaction with a 500, and the sender retries.

panels.title: Upstream unreachable (window)
panels.description: Requests the Python inbound worker could not be reached for.

panels.title: Transactions by route and reason
panels.description: Where each transaction went (native, proxy, abandoned) and why. Proxy reasons: mode_proxy/mode_shadow (the mode), has_pdus, malformed, limits, auth_failed, origin_in_backoff, canary_not_selected, uncertain, db_error, too_large, not_send.

panels.title: Latency by route
panels.description: Time to answer, by route. Proxied latency is mostly the Python worker's.

panels.title: EDUs by type and action
panels.description: Every EDU decided, natively or in shadow: forwarded, dropped as untracked presence, or dropped by a room's server ACL. edu_type="other" is a type Synapse has no handler for; the log names the first of each.

panels.title: EDUs forwarded, by destination writer
panels.description: Forwards by stream writer. In shadow, set this beside the Synapse panel below: the counts should match what the Python worker sends.

panels.title: Forward latency
panels.description: One EDU handed to its writer over replication, retries included.

panels.title: Forwards by outcome
panels.description: ok, error (a non-retryable answer) or timeout (gave up after retrying).

panels.title: Replication retries and ACL removals
panels.description: Retries of a forward (timeout or connection refused), and rooms removed from receipt EDUs by server ACL.

panels.title: Shadow decisions
panels.description: For each transaction Synapse handled, what native mode would have done, and why not when it would have proxied.

panels.title: Disagreements and dropped evaluations
panels.description: Disagreements by Synapse's status; evaluations dropped because the shadow queue was full.

panels.title: PDU checks by outcome
panels.description: Each PDU Synapse accepted, once persisted: 'signatures' (event ID, content hash, signatures), 'state_auth' (state resolution, auth verdict, resulting state), 'soft_fail' and 'push' (push action rows). 'received' covers PDUs that never got that far. Any mismatch is a disagreement with Synapse worth reading in the log.

panels.title: Skipped, by reason
panels.description: Events the comparison cannot be made for: outliers, prevs without state groups, prev state computed after the event's (Synapse used a remote's state), keys reissued since, room v1.

panels.title: Time for Synapse to persist a PDU
panels.description: From receipt to the event appearing in Synapse's database; the shadow waits for it.

panels.title: PDU shadow dropped and chain link batches
panels.description: PDUs not checked because the queue was full; and how many chain link batches Synapse would need per auth difference (above 1, Synapse's own v2.1 answer depends on set order).

panels.title: PDU checker memory
panels.description: Resident memory, and the state group cache: its entries (~210 bytes each, bounded by pdu_shadow.state_cache_entries) and how groups were got. 'delta' is a group rebuilt from its cached prev group; 'full' a read of the whole group, 150k rows in a big room.

panels.title: Synapse: EDUs received over replication, by writer
panels.description: ReplicationFederationSendEduRestServlet on each Synapse instance: every EDU forwarded to it, from the Python worker or from us. Moving to native must not change this.

panels.title: Synapse: /send reaching the Python worker
panels.description: FederationSendServlet on the Python inbound worker. Falls by ~96% once EDU-only transactions are native.

panels.title: Synapse: inbound EDUs and PDUs at the Python worker
panels.description: What the Python worker still parses.

panels.title: Queries by name and result
panels.description: Every query is a primary-key lookup: txn_state once per native transaction, current_server_acl for typing and receipts (cached 5s per room), server_keys on a key-cache miss.

panels.title: ACL lookups by source
panels.description: cached, db, error, redacted (a redacted ACL sends the transaction to Synapse).

panels.title: Process: goinbound vs the Python inbound worker
CPU
panels.description: Cores used.

panels.title: Goroutines and restarts
panels.description: Goroutines should track request concurrency, not grow. A restart is a step in process_start_time_seconds.
